items.question: What is Planwise and how can it help me?
items.answer: Planwise is a premium coordination and planning service for ageing well. We assess your needs and wants, make recommendations, help you understand your options, and connect with suitable services when needed.

items.question: Who is Planwise for?
items.answer: Planwise supports older Australians planning ahead, families supporting loved ones, and anyone looking for independent guidance about later life decisions and ageing well.

items.question: What does Planwise cost?
items.answer: We offer three ways to work with us: Planwise Partner at $49 per month (minimum 3 months), Family Navigator at $79 per month (minimum 6 months) for up to 3 family members, or the Ageing Well Comprehensive Package at $495 one-off. A free 15-minute discovery call is available to discuss your needs and the right option for you.

items.question: Is Planwise independent from providers?
items.answer: Yes. Planwise does not receive commissions from aged care providers or any referral partners from our quality referral network. This allows us to provide guidance based on your circumstances and preferences.

items.question: Do I need to be receiving aged care services to use Planwise?
items.answer: No. You can work with Planwise before you need aged care services. Many people start planning earlier to understand their options and prepare for the future.

items.question: Who runs Planwise?
items.answer: Planwise is led by a Registered Nurse and a Registered Psychologist with experience in care coordination, healthy ageing and supporting older Australians through later life planning.

items.question: How do you choose the providers you recommend?
items.answer: We recommend providers after understanding your needs, goals and preferences. Recommendations are based on suitability and are never influenced by commissions or commercial arrangements. We have vetted the services and providers that make up our referral network. We also welcome feedback from our clients about their experience with services we have recommended, so we can maintain the high quality our clients expect.

items.question: How do I contact Planwise?
items.answer: You can contact us by phone, email or by completing the enquiry form on this page. You can also book a free 15-minute discovery call online.

items.question: How do I book a free discovery call?
items.answer: Simply use the booking button on this page to choose a time that suits you. If you prefer, you can also contact us by phone or email to arrange a call.

items.question: Do you offer a free consultation?
items.answer: Yes. We offer a free 15-minute discovery call to help you discuss your situation, ask questions and learn how Planwise can support you.

items.question: Can family members contact Planwise?
items.answer: Yes. We regularly support adult children, spouses, carers and other family members who are helping an older loved one plan for later life.

items.question: Do you help people outside Melbourne?
items.answer: Yes. Depending on your location and needs, we can provide support by phone or video. Contact us to discuss the most suitable option.

items.question: How much does Planwise cost?
items.answer: We offer three ways to work with us: Planwise Partner for $49 per month (minimum 3 months), Family Navigator for $79 per month (minimum 6 months) for up to 3 family members, or the Ageing Well Comprehensive Package for $495 one-off. Every plan starts with a free 15-minute discovery call.

items.question: Which membership is right for me?
items.answer: That depends on the level of support you need. If you have a specific question or decision, on-demand support may be suitable. If you'd like ongoing guidance, a membership may be the better option.

items.question: Is there a free option to start?
items.answer: Yes. We offer a free 15-minute discovery call so you can discuss your situation, ask questions and decide whether Planwise is right for you.

items.question: Can I cancel my membership?
items.answer: Please refer to your membership agreement or speak with the Planwise team for information about cancellation terms and ongoing support options.

items.question: Do you receive commissions from providers?
items.answer: No. Planwise does not receive commissions or referral incentives from aged care providers. Our recommendations are based solely on your circumstances and goals.

items.question: What are the 4 Pillars of Ageing Well?
items.answer: The 4 Pillars of Ageing Well are Purpose, Legal & Financial, Mind & Body, and Where & How You Live. Together, they provide a framework for planning later life and considering the different factors that contribute to wellbeing and independence.

items.question: What does ageing well actually mean?
items.answer: Ageing well means maintaining your wellbeing, independence and quality of life as your needs and circumstances change. It involves more than health alone and includes your relationships, living arrangements, financial planning and sense of purpose.

items.question: Do I have to use all four pillars?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Some people may focus on one area, while others benefit from considering all four. The framework is flexible and designed to reflect your individual circumstances and priorities.

items.question: Are these real client stories?
items.answer: Yes. These stories are based on real experiences of people and families who have worked with Planwise. We only share client stories with permission or after removing names and identifying details to protect privacy.

items.question: Can Planwise help if I'm planning ahead?
items.answer: Yes. Many people work with us before they need aged care services or additional support. Planning ahead can help you understand your options and prepare for future decisions.

items.question: Can you help if I'm supporting an ageing parent?
items.answer: Yes. We regularly work with adult children, partners and other family members to help them understand options and make informed decisions together.

items.question: What kinds of situations does Planwise help with?
items.answer: We support people with a wide range of later life decisions, including planning ahead, finding purpose and direction after retirement, home support, aged care, housing, staying connected to community, and accessing trusted services.

items.question: Do I have to research everything myself?
items.answer: No. There's a huge amount of information available about ageing, aged care, and later life planning, and working out what's actually relevant to your situation takes time. We've already done that groundwork, so instead of spending hours piecing it together yourself, you get guidance and options that are already relevant to you.

items.question: Can you help if I don't know where to start?
items.answer: Yes. Many people contact us because they're unsure about their options. We'll take the time to understand your situation and help you identify the next steps that are right for you. We are available to answer your questions whenever they arise.

items.question: How do I get started?
items.answer: Start with a free discovery call. We'll discuss your situation, answer your questions and help you decide which level of support is right for you.
